access.edition_or_version: Speaking of Siva, trans. A. K. Ramanujan (Penguin Classics, 1973)

mechanics.tone_relevance: Non-Anglophone anchor for intimate address in a plainspoken register: the speaker addresses Siva by a personal local name ('lord of the meeting rivers').
mechanics.point_of_view: First person, addressed to a named deity; the 'I-thou' frame is sustained across short free-verse sayings.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Free verse, concrete workaday imagery (the body as shrine, the moving and the standing), proverbial plainness, signature address at the close.
mechanics.dialogue: Devotional address functions as intimate conversation with a named lord rather than formal praise.
mechanics.register: Anti-formal, anti-courtly colloquial Kannada; intimacy is produced by plainness and direct naming.
mechanics.intimacy_technique: Intimate address without mystification; the deity is spoken to as a familiar local presence.
mechanics.translation_note: Medieval Kannada free verse into English; oral cadence and the signature address are approximated, not reproduced.
mechanics.copyright_note: Translation copyrighted; source poems traditional. Techniques described, no text reproduced.
